fields.label: Encrypt
fields.description: TLS negotiation with SQL Server. Use disable for clear text, false for login-only encryption unless the server requires more, true for encrypted traffic, or strict for TDS 8.0 with certificate verification.

fields.label: Skip TLS Verify
fields.description: Skip server certificate verification when encryption is true.

fields.label: TLS/SSL Root Certificate
fields.description: Path on the Grafana server to a .pem or .der certificate authority file used to verify SQL Server.

fields.label: Hostname in server certificate
fields.description: Host name to verify in the SQL Server certificate.

fields.label: Authentication Type
fields.description: SQL Server Authentication is the default. For a direct Kerberos cache, select Windows AD: Credential cache. For a JSON lookup file, select Windows AD: Credential cache file. Azure AD Authentication uses the nested jsonData.azureCredentials object.

fields.label: Username
fields.description: SQL login name or Windows AD principal. Use user@REALM for Kerberos.
fields.dependsOn: !has(jsonData.authenticationType) || jsonData.authenticationType in ['', 'SQL Server Authentication', 'Windows AD: Username + password', 'Windows AD: Keytab', 'Windows AD: Credential cache file']
fields.requiredWhen: !has(jsonData.authenticationType) || jsonData.authenticationType in ['', 'SQL Server Authentication', 'Windows AD: Username + password', 'Windows AD: Keytab', 'Windows AD: Credential cache file']

fields.label: Password
fields.dependsOn: !has(jsonData.authenticationType) || jsonData.authenticationType in ['', 'SQL Server Authentication', 'Windows AD: Username + password'] || (jsonData.authenticationType == 'Azure AD Authentication' && 'ad-password' == azure.authType)
fields.requiredWhen: !has(jsonData.authenticationType) || jsonData.authenticationType in ['', 'SQL Server Authentication', 'Windows AD: Username + password'] || (jsonData.authenticationType == 'Azure AD Authentication' && 'ad-password' == azure.authType)
fields.description: Password for the SQL login, Kerberos principal or Azure Entra user.

fields.label: Keytab file path
fields.description: Path on the Grafana server to the keytab for the Kerberos principal.

fields.label: Credential cache path
fields.description: Direct path to the Kerberos credential cache on the Grafana server, such as /tmp/krb5cc_1000. Select Windows AD: Credential cache.

fields.label: Credential cache file path
fields.description: Path to a JSON lookup file that maps the Kerberos user, SQL database and server address to a credential cache. Select Windows AD: Credential cache file.

fields.label: Authentication type
fields.description: Store this choice at jsonData.azureCredentials.authType. For Managed Identity set azureCredentials to {"authType":"msi"}. For Azure Entra Password set authType to ad-password and put clientId and userId in that same object. Grafana settings enable Managed Identity and Entra Password. Current User appears when Entra Password and user identity are enabled.

fields.label: Azure Cloud
fields.description: Set jsonData.azureCredentials.azureCloud explicitly when provisioning an app registration. The editor initializes this field from Grafana's Azure cloud setting and offers only the public Azure cloud (AzureCloud) in the dropdown.

fields.label: Directory (tenant) ID
fields.description: Microsoft Entra tenant ID of the app registration, stored in jsonData.azureCredentials.tenantId.

fields.label: Application (client) ID
fields.dependsOn: (jsonData.authenticationType == 'Azure AD Authentication' && azure.authType == 'clientsecret') || (jsonData.authenticationType == 'Azure AD Authentication' && azure.authType == 'ad-password')
fields.requiredWhen: (jsonData.authenticationType == 'Azure AD Authentication' && azure.authType == 'clientsecret') || (jsonData.authenticationType == 'Azure AD Authentication' && azure.authType == 'ad-password')
fields.description: Application client ID stored in jsonData.azureCredentials.clientId.

fields.label: User ID
fields.description: Microsoft Entra sign-in username for password authentication, such as user@contoso.onmicrosoft.com. Store it in jsonData.azureCredentials.userId.

fields.label: Client Secret
fields.description: Client secret of the app registration.

fields.label: Legacy Azure client secret
fields.description: Fallback for migrated app registrations when azureClientSecret has never been set.

fields.label: Forward OAuth Identity
fields.description: Forward the signed-in user’s identity token to SQL Server. Set to true for Current User.

fields.label: Disable Grafana cache
fields.description: Disable Grafana data caching for Current User to keep results specific to each identity.

fields.label: krb5 config file path
fields.description: Path to the Kerberos configuration on the Grafana server. If unset, the driver uses KRB5_CONFIG, then /etc/krb5.conf.

fields.label: UDP Preference Limit
fields.description: Whole-number UDP size threshold in bytes for Kerberos requests. Set to 1 to always use TCP.

fields.label: DNS Lookup KDC
fields.description: String boolean that controls DNS SRV lookups of Kerberos key distribution centers. Defaults to true.

fields.label: Auto max idle
fields.description: Keep the idle limit in sync when editing the open connection limit. New connections start in auto mode. If pool limits already exist, a missing switch means manual mode. In provisioning, set maxIdleConns explicitly.

fields.label: Max open
fields.description: Maximum open connections as a whole number. Zero removes the limit. If omitted, Grafana supplies its configured default.

fields.label: Max idle
fields.description: Maximum idle connections as a whole number. Zero retains none. If omitted, Grafana supplies its configured default.

fields.label: Max lifetime
fields.description: Maximum lifetime of a connection in whole seconds. Zero removes the lifetime limit. If omitted, Grafana supplies its configured default.

fields.label: Connection timeout
fields.description: Time to wait for a SQL connection in whole seconds. Zero leaves the connection timeout unset.

fields.label: Proxy username
fields.description: SOCKS proxy username. Defaults to the data source UID.

fields.label: Proxy password
fields.description: Password for the secure SOCKS proxy.

fields.label: Proxy timeout
fields.description: Time in seconds to establish a connection through the secure SOCKS proxy.

fields.label: Proxy keep-alive
fields.description: TCP keep-alive interval in seconds for the secure SOCKS proxy.

sqleng_settings.url.label: Host
sqleng_settings.url.description: SQL Server host or named instance with an optional port, such as localhost:1433. Omit the URL scheme.

sqleng_settings.timeInterval.label: Min time interval
sqleng_settings.timeInterval.description: Lower limit for the automatic group-by interval, such as 1m.

sqleng_settings.enableSecureSocksProxy.label: Enabled
sqleng_settings.enableSecureSocksProxy.description: Route SQL connections through the private data source connection configured in Grafana. Available when the secure SOCKS proxy is enabled on the server.

sqleng_settings.database.label: Database
sqleng_settings.database.description: Name of the SQL Server database to query. Older configurations may store the name in the root database field, which the editor migrates here.

instructions.msg: For Azure AD Authentication, nest authType and its public fields inside jsonData.azureCredentials. For Current User, also set jsonData.oauthPassThru and jsonData.disableGrafanaCache to true. For SQL Server Authentication or Windows AD username/password, put user at the data source root and password in secureJsonData.
